title: First Annual Explicit Teaching Institute
author: Zach Groshell
summary: Groshell recaps the first-ever Explicit Teaching Institute, a professional development event held at the Inwood Academy for Leadership in NYC that brought educators together to bridge cognitive science research and daily classroom practice. Participants practiced high-leverage techniques including choral response and turn-and-talk routines for engaging the whole room simultaneously, systematic checking for understanding in place of vague 'does that make sense' prompts, and precision scripting to pre-plan core explanations and reduce filler and confusion. The piece is built substantially from participant testimonials, which credit the institute for grounding every strategy in modeling, practice, and rehearsal rather than theory alone, and for tying the week's content explicitly back to Project Follow Through and Groshell's own book on explicit instruction.
points: Choral response and turn-and-talk were framed as routines for engaging 100 percent of the room simultaneously, not just occasional participation techniques.
Checking for understanding was reframed away from the vague 'does that make sense?' prompt toward systematic, immediate checks that actually verify comprehension.
Precision scripting — mapping out core explanations in advance — was taught as a way to reduce filler words and confusion during instruction.
Participant Kimberly Konzack singled out the institute for going 'far beyond theory,' with every strategy modeled, explained, practiced, and rehearsed rather than just presented.

The institute opened with Project Follow Through, giving participants a historical evidentiary anchor for why explicit instruction techniques were being taught before moving into the techniques themselves.
quotes: This intensive professional development event brought together an incredible group of educators who are truly passionate about bridging the gap between cognitive science and daily classroom practice.

Checking for Understanding: Shifting away from "Does that make sense?" toward systemic, immediate checks. Precision Scripting: Learning to map out core explanations beforehand to reduce filler words and confusion.

The Explicit Teaching Institute in Inwood, NY was one of the most practical and impactful professional learning experiences I've attended. Zach Groshell and the team created an experience that went far beyond theory. Every strategy was modeled, explained, practiced, rehearsed, and discussed, so I left not only understanding explicit instruction, but feeling confident implementing it in my own classroom.
I liked how you started with Project Follow Through and always gave the why behind the strategies. Day 3 with the retrieval and opportunities to respond was really good.

Much of the information was affirmation for me based on previous experience with Anita Archer and TLAC. I loved the crisp, clear, replicable routines and the practice opportunities. I also loved the use of models / incorrect examples to create a set of success criteria that can be used as a checklist during independent work/grading.
